# Part 1 · Import the same data two ways

**▶ Run this in your Script:**

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)

pine_csv_df   <- read_csv("data/pine_needles.csv")
pine_excel_df <- read_excel("data/pine_needles.xlsx")
```

# Part 2b · `filter()` — OR, `%in%`, and missing values

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
# OR: shady side, OR any exceptionally long needle
pine_csv_df |> filter(n_s == "n" | length_mm > 22)

# %in%: match one of several named teams
pine_csv_df |> filter(group %in% c("cephalopods", "salmon"))
```

# Part 4b · `case_when()` — recoding and binning

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
pine_csv_df |>
  mutate(
    size_class = case_when(
      length_mm < 16 ~ "short",
      length_mm < 20 ~ "medium",
      TRUE           ~ "long"
    )
  ) |>
  count(size_class)
```

# Part 6 · The full pipeline

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
pine_wrangled_df <- pine_csv_df |>
  filter(length_mm > 0) |>
  select(group, n_s, sun, length_mm) |>
  mutate(
    length_cm  = length_mm / 10,
    log_length = log(length_mm),
    size_class = case_when(
      length_mm < 16 ~ "short",
      length_mm < 20 ~ "medium",
      TRUE           ~ "long"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(n_s, desc(length_mm))

head(pine_wrangled_df)
```

# Part 7 · Finding duplicate rows

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
needle_check_df <- read_csv("data/pine_needles_error.csv")

nrow(needle_check_df)
n_distinct(needle_check_df)
```

✏️ **Your turn:** Do `nrow()` and `n_distinct()` match? What does that tell you? `________________________`

**▶ Run this:**

``` r
needle_check_df |> filter(duplicated(needle_check_df))

needle_clean_df <- needle_check_df |> distinct()

nrow(needle_clean_df)
```

✏️ **Your turn:** How many rows did `distinct()` remove? Why does this matter for the sample size you'd report? `________________________`

> ⚠️ **Watch out!** `distinct()` only catches *exact* duplicate rows — a mistyped name won't be caught. Always look at your data too.

# Part 9 · Review and checkpoint

At this point you can:

- [ ] Read the same dataset from a `.csv` and an `.xlsx`
- [ ] Use `filter()`, `select()`, `mutate()`, and `arrange()` on real data
- [ ] Filter with `%in%`, `is.na()`/`!is.na()`, and both AND (`,`) and OR (`|`)
- [ ] Recode or bin a column with `case_when()`, including a `TRUE ~` catch-all
- [ ] Add a unit-converted column and a log-transformed column with `mutate()`
- [ ] Chain multiple verbs into one pipeline with `|>`
- [ ] Check for duplicate rows with `nrow()` / `n_distinct()`, and remove them with `distinct()`
- [ ] Save a new file with `write_csv()` without touching the raw data

# Getting unstuck

When code breaks — and it will, that is normal:

1.  **Read the error message out loud.** R usually names the line and the problem.
2.  **Check the usual suspects:** did you run `library(tidyverse)` and `library(readxl)`? Spelling? A missing `)` or a `|>` at the *start* of a line?
3.  `?function_name` opens the built-in help page.
4.  **Bring the exact error** (copy-paste it) to class or office hours.

> 💡 **Key idea:** Every working scientist googles error messages daily. Getting stuck is not failing — it is the job.
